items.item: Uses a Named Credential (callout:...) instead of a hard-coded URL or credentials
items.evidence: ENDPOINT = 'callout:ERP/api/orders'; notes explain creating a Named Credential called ERP

items.item: Makes the callout asynchronously (Queueable with Database.AllowsCallouts or @future(callout=true)), not directly in the trigger transaction
items.evidence: System.enqueueJob(new PostOrdersJob(orderIds)); class PostOrdersJob implements Queueable, Database.AllowsCallouts

items.item: Includes a test that uses HttpCalloutMock with Test.setMock, covering a failure response
items.evidence: Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MockErp(500)); nonSuccessResponseThrows asserts ErpException contains '500'
